messages:
anya: heads-up 1; ran burst harness and hit an allocator fallback->preempt loop that spiked tenant throttles.
anya: repro: `go test ./orchestrator -run TestShardFallbackPreemptLoop`
anya: log excerpt:
2026-03-10T09:12:01Z INFO admission: admit shard=shard-9 tenant=tn-9 tokens=256
2026-03-10T09:12:01Z WARN preempt: evict shard=shard-9 reason=preemptible-credit-exhausted
2026-03-10T09:12:01Z INFO fallback: reroute req=aa1 -> shard-21
2026-03-10T09:12:01Z WARN preempt: evict shard=shard-21 reason=hotspot
2026-03-10T09:12:02Z ERROR admission: tenant throttle spike rate=480/s

sam: config used? headroom/burst/eviction-priority?
anya: headroom=3, burst_credits=80, preemptible=true, eviction_priority:{burst:4,preemptible:9}.
julia: looks like fallback policy ignores recent eviction history and picks small shards that just got evicted -> immediate reassign -> oscillation.
mike: options: (1) per-shard cooldown after eviction, (2) prefer shards with low recent_preempt_rate, (3) add a tiny jitter/delay before reassign.
anya: cooldown seems easiest to reason about.
sam: but long cooldown reduces fallback capacity. we need to detect real "flapping" vs normal churn.
julia: proposal: flapping detector using preempt_count_1m and reassigns_30s thresholds. mark shard as flapping -> deprioritize in fallback for Xs.
mike: tie cooldown to eviction type: preemptible -> 5-15s, hotspot/oom -> 30-120s.
anya: should allocator emit a metric when many fallbacks happen so the autoscaler can react?
sam: yes: emit `fallback_amplification` and have scaler convert to low-confidence scale intent if it breaches threshold; that avoids silent autoscale spikes.
julia: also add an SDK hint `prefer_stable_shard=true` for clients that can tolerate slightly higher latency but avoid retries.
mike: rollout plan: implement flapping detector + cooldown behind FF, emit metric, add SDK hint, run canary for 48h against the sim cluster.
anya: I'll draft the mini-RFC with thresholds, a sim harness, and unit tests. ping @orch-bot on PR.
